title: Do Deterministic Verifiers Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Paired Shared‑Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) to measure whether coupling a deterministic NetOps verifier+gate (generate→validate→repair, max 1 automated repair) to a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) changes safety outcomes when the identical initial LLM candidate is observed with and without gating. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled generation reused for both arms per intent), we evaluated 200 deterministically selected paired intents in a sandboxed Batfish-style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). All 200 shared initial candidates passed validation in both baseline and guarded arms (contingency: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered paired estimand (guarded minus baseline unsafe-proposal rate) = 0.0; exact two-sided p = 1.0; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). No automated repairs were applied. We document the preregistered design, execution accounting, artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null, and concrete artifact-supported recommendations for follow-up designs that avoid ceiling effects.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and maintenance workflows for NetOps and AIOps. Operational adoption hinges on quantitative evidence that model-generated changes will not introduce reachability or policy violations when applied. Prior surveys and empirical reports stress that operational trustworthiness depends heavily on surrounding system machinery—retrieval, deterministic validators, gates, and repair loops—rather than on the model alone [1],[2]. Architectures that chain generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair (generate→validate→repair) are widely advocated, but paired evidence that isolates the validator/gate effect on identical model candidates is limited [3],[4].

Research question. For an intent→configuration task bank and a single LLM, does coupling a deterministic validator and deterministic accept/reject gate (with at most one automated repair attempt) to the identical sampled initial candidate reduce the incidence of unsafe proposals relative to observing that same candidate without gating? We operationalized this question as the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics and executed a fixed-sample paired experiment (n=200 pairs).

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired design and frozen execution (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) fixing generation semantics, sampling, model, validator, gating policy, and analysis prior to observation; (2) an autonomous confirmatory run using gpt-5-mini and a Batfish-style deterministic validator on n=200 deterministically selected paired intents with shared_initial_candidate semantics; (3) artifact-grounded analysis showing complete concordance (all candidates valid), discussion of ceiling effects and their artifact-supported causes, and concrete, artifact-supported recommendations for follow-up confirmatory designs that can produce nondegenerate inference of verifier/gate value.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and AIOps work covers intent-based configuration, runbook generation, root-cause analysis, and early agentic self-healing proposals. Several recent surveys and empirical reports document hallucination and unsafe command risks and recommend validator-coupled pipelines and knowledge anchoring to mitigate such risks [1],[3],[5]. Generate–validate–repair and guarded-agent architectures are echoed across adjacent domains (program repair, DevOps) where external deterministic checks and sandboxed emulation reduce unsafe outputs in practice [6],[7].

Methodological gaps. Two persistent gaps motivated our design choice. First, many prior comparisons use nonpaired samples or permit different generation semantics per arm, making it difficult to attribute safety gains specifically to validators rather than to differing model draws. Second, existing benchmarks frequently focus on QA/relevance or log-analysis metrics and lack tightly coupled intent→config items evaluated under deterministic validators and paired protocols that preserve initial-candidate sampling variance [2],[5]. Our preregistered shared_initial_candidate experiment isolates validator/repair/gate effects on identical first-pass candidates and thus addresses a tightly specified methodological question in this space.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered the study as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 and froze the primary estimand, generation semantics, model/adapter, deterministic validator and gate policy, repair budget, deterministic task-selection rule, sample size (task_count = 200 paired intents), and the confirmatory analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration and execution manifest are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.

Generation semantics clarification (preregistered and executed). The executed generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded arms per paired intent. Therefore the confirmatory estimand evaluates only validator/repair/gate effects on that identical first-pass candidate and does not measure any effect of guarded-conditioned regeneration, independent regeneration, or model-sampling variance. This semantics choice was preregistered and recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and the execution manifest.

Models, adapter, validator, and decision policy. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and provider = "openai_responses"). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5, implementing Batfish-style sequencing, reachability, protected-interface, and workflow-precondition checks. Gate policy: deterministic accept/reject according to validator outcome; if a violation was found, the gate allowed up to one automated repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) as preregistered.

Task bank and deterministic sampling. The task bank used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to synthesize intent→configuration pairs with encoded initial_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies, and difficulty metadata. Sampling followed a fixed adapter index rule (task_count = 200 pairs; planned_episode_count = 400) described in the preregistration; selection is deterministic and outcome-independent. Manifest metadata indicates the bank is dominated by items labeled 'very_hard' with a minority labeled 'extreme'; exact per-label counts are available in the archived task_manifest.jsonl.

Primary outcome and scoring. The primary binary outcome unsafe_flag was set when the deterministic validator reported any reachability or workflow/policy violation after the candidate stabilized (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Scoring reason codes, validator traces (validation_before/validation_after), repair flags, and normalized configurations were archived under execution/scoring/*. Representative scoring artifacts are included in the evidence bundle. Repair activity was permitted but bounded to one automated attempt per pair.

Confirmatory analysis (frozen). The preregistered analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1 comparing unsafe_flag across paired conditions. The analysis reports discordant pair counts (n10 = guarded_only unsafe; n01 = baseline_only unsafe), an exact two-sided McNemar-equivalent p-value, and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). Missingness policy was complete_pair_primary (drop pair if a condition failed due to infrastructure); the run produced zero retriable infrastructure failures.

Implementation and archival hygiene. All model provider traces, shared_initial generation artifacts, per-episode responses, validator traces, repair traces (null when unused), task_manifest.jsonl, and analysis outputs (analysis/results.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) were recorded and archived during execution. Representative artifact paths are execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/responses/*.txt, execution/provider_calls/*.json, and execution/scoring/*.json. Deterministic reconciliation and provider call audits are stored under analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run executed as preregistered: started_at_utc = 2026-08-31T13:49:34.191203+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026-08-31T14:14:32.660268+00:00 (execution manifest). Planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, and cache_hit_count = 0. All deterministic consistency checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Thus every shared initial candidate was scored VALID_CONFIGURATION by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in both arms. The paired estimate (guarded minus baseline unsafe-proposal rate) = 0.0. Exact two-sided test returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI is [0.0, 0.0], computed with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The zero-width CI results from complete concordance (no discordant pairs) under the registered estimand.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; repair_provider_trace_path fields are null in all scoring artifacts. Validator traces per episode record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and final_state snapshots. Representative episodes (task-000004 through task-000008) in execution/scoring/* show required sequences were parsed and validator reported violation_count = 0 and empty violations arrays for all completed episodes. The validator's scoring_reason_code is VALID_CONFIGURATION for every scoring record.

Latency and operational notes. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics required a single model call per pair, model_call accounting equals 200. Guarded pipeline wall time included deterministic validator execution but no repair cycles; timing logs in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl show median additional per-pair wall time dominated by validator evaluation rather than repair attempts. Exact latency distributions are archived and reproducible from execution/execution_log.jsonl.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. missingness_summary shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. contamination_summary.csv is empty. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode_accounting_consistent = true and provider call audit consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Representative task patterns. Tasks exercised sequencing constraints (safe VLAN migration, uplink failover, MTU upgrades), protected interfaces (mgmt1), final_group constraints, and minimum-up requirements. For example, task-000004 required a four-step sequence (edge2 down → vlan 40 → edge2 up → edge1 down) and the validator normalized and accepted the shared initial candidate (execution/scoring/task-000004-*.json). These artifacts illustrate validator coverage of sequencing and precondition rules used to define unsafe_flag.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the confirmatory estimand isolates only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first-pass candidates. Observing n11 = 200 (every shared initial candidate valid) implies that, for the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), the selected synthetic task bank, the prompt/template family used, and the deterministic validator's ruleset, the sampled initial candidates already satisfied the validator constraints; therefore the guarded machinery applied no repairs and changed no acceptance decisions. The archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and execution/scoring/*.json) directly support this artifact-grounded interpretation.

Why the paired-bootstrap CI is zero-width. The paired-bootstrap CI is degenerate because there are no discordant pairs to resample; every bootstrap resample of paired outcomes yields the same paired difference (0.0). This produces zero empirical variance and therefore a CI [0.0,0.0]. The analysis executor parameters and seed (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) are archived and reproduce this result exactly (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Ceiling-effect contributors, supported by artifacts. Three artifact-supported contributors to the ceiling effect are (1) task design alignment: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced intents whose required sequences closely match the prompt schema and model output form; (2) validator tightness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encoded sequencing and precondition checks that match the generator's reference-answer construction; and (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics prevented any guarded-conditioned regeneration or model variance that might have produced repairs or discordant outcomes. These contributors are evident in the task_manifest entries and representative validator traces archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json.

Design recommendations grounded in execution artifacts. To produce a nondegenerate confirmatory comparison of verifier/gate effectiveness, we recommend (a) augmenting the task bank with adversarial or out-of-distribution intents to raise baseline unsafe rates (the archived task_manifest.jsonl contains generation seeds and difficulty metadata and is the natural insertion point for adversarial seeds); (b) running an alternative confirmatory design that uses independent generation per condition or multiple independent samples per condition (this changes the estimand and increases model_call budget requirements); (c) testing multiple model variants, sampling temperatures, or decoding settings to expose model sampling variance (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model and temperature fields); (d) increasing automated repair budget or enabling iterative repair loops to evaluate repair effectiveness under substantive initial violations; and (e) including human-in-the-loop arms to study operator behavior on validator-flagged candidates. Each recommendation maps to concrete artifact locations for reproducible follow-up (e.g., execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

Threats to validity and generalizability. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally limit inference to validator/gate effects and exclude guarded-conditioned regeneration effects. Construct validity: unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage of sequencing and precondition rules and therefore does not capture all operational hazards (for example, transient performance regressions or vendor-specific side effects outside validator rules). External validity: single model, single validator, synthetic tasks, and sandboxed validation limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: the run was powered to detect ~10 percentage-point paired reductions per the preregistration power plan, but the observed concordance precludes observing reductions because baseline unsafe occurrences were absent. All of these threats are documented and traceable to archived preregistration and execution artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing an LLM-alone observation to that same initial candidate after deterministic verification and bounded automated repair. Every sampled initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator and the guarded pipeline applied no repairs; the paired difference = 0.0 (p = 1.0) with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. This null result is specific to the chosen model, synthetic task bank, deterministic selection, validator ruleset, and shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not contradict prior evidence that validators can reduce unsafe outputs under different experimental regimes (e.g., independent condition generation, adversarial inputs, multiple model samples). We archive full artifacts and recommend follow-up preregistered designs that intentionally increase baseline unsafe rates or permit independent per-condition generation to quantify verifier/gate contributions under more challenging conditions. All core artifacts and analysis outputs supporting these conclusions are archived and referenced in the manuscript evidence bundle.

limitations: Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics mean baseline and guarded conditions began from an identical initial candidate; the confirmatory estimand therefore measures only validator/repair/gate effects on that same candidate and cannot assess effects of guarded-conditioned regeneration or prompt engineering.

Construct validity: tasks were synthetic and deterministically selected; the binary unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage (reachability and workflow sequencing rules) and may not capture other operational risks (transient performance regressions, vendor-specific side effects outside validator rules).

External validity: a single LLM (gpt-5-mini), a single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions.

Conclusion validity: the observed null effect (paired difference = 0) reflects this execution's sampling frame where baseline generation produced only valid candidates; the study was powered to detect ~10 percentage-point reductions but cannot rule out smaller effects under different sampling or adversarial inputs.
Operational relevance: no live device changes were executed (sandboxed validation only); operational benefits (reduced triage time, deployment safety) were not measured.
Security/contamination: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; no retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) was used, so retrieval-based poisoning vectors were not evaluated.

Task-bank reporting: the archived task_manifest.jsonl is authoritative for per-label counts; manifest metadata indicates tasks are dominated by 'very_hard' items with a minority labeled 'extreme' (exact per-label counts are available in the archived manifest).
